report:
Contrary to your expectation, robust clinical trial evidence demonstrates that **denosumab (Prolia) significantly reduces the risk of vertebral fractures** in patients with osteoporosis.

### The Evidence
The primary evidence comes from the landmark Phase 3 **FREEDOM trial** published in *The New England Journal of Medicine*:
* **Vertebral Fracture Reduction:** Subcutaneous administration of 60 mg denosumab every 6 months reduced the relative risk of new vertebral fractures by **68%** over 3 years compared to placebo (2.3% in the denosumab group vs. 7.2% in the placebo group).
* **Broad Efficacy:** It also significantly reduced the risk of hip fractures (by 40%) and non-vertebral fractures (by 20%).

Long-term follow-up studies and meta-analyses confirm that ongoing treatment with denosumab maintains bone mineral density gains and sustained fracture prevention.

### Important Distinction: Rebound Risk Upon Discontinuation
Confusion regarding denosumab and vertebral fractures often arises from what happens when treatment is **stopped**. Discontinuing denosumab causes a rapid rebound increase in bone turnover, leading to accelerated bone loss and an elevated risk of *rebound multiple vertebral fractures*. Because of this rebound effect, clinical guidelines stress that denosumab must not be stopped without transitioning to another anti-resorptive drug (such as a bisphosphonate).

### Conclusion
When taken continuously as prescribed, denosumab is a highly effective treatment for lowering vertebral fracture risk in osteoporosis.

### Sources
* NEJM FREEDOM Trial: https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493
* American Academy of Family Physicians: https://www.aafp.org/afp/2019/0501/od1
* PMC Denosumab 10-Year Review: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8799550/
* FDA Prolia Prescribing Information: https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2011/125320s5s6lbl.pdf
